span.label: mechanisms
span.term: masked language modeling: randomly mask tokens and train the model to predict them from both left and right context, giving a deep bidirectional representation that transfers to many tasks via fine-tuning
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Masking creates a mismatch between pre-training and fine-tuning because [MASK] never appears downstream.
span.note: what this limits: any account of what the pre-trained model has learned to expect: WE ARE CREATING A MISMATCH BETWEEN PRE-TRAINING AND FINE-TUNING, SINCE THE [MASK] TOKEN DOES NOT APPEAR DURING FINE-TUNING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The [CLS] vector is not usable as a sentence representation without fine-tuning.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the [CLS] vector as a sentence embedding without fine-tuning: THE VECTOR C IS NOT A MEANINGFUL SENTENCE REPRESENTATION WITHOUT FINE-TUNING, SINCE IT WAS TRAINED WITH NSP
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Fine-tuning the large model was unstable on small datasets and required multiple random restarts.
span.note: what this limits: the reported small-dataset results: FOR BERT_LARGE WE FOUND THAT FINETUNING WAS SOMETIMES UNSTABLE ON SMALL DATASETS, SO WE RAN SEVERAL RANDOM RESTARTS AND SELECTED THE BEST MODEL ON THE DEV SET
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reported average is not the official score of the benchmark it is reported on.
span.note: what this limits: the GLUE averages quoted from this table: the authors state the Average column is slightly different from the official GLUE score because the WNLI set is excluded, so it is not comparable with an official GLUE average
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The pre-training objective is an existing task under a new name, which the authors state.
span.note: what this limits: any claim of novelty for the masked LM objective: the authors note the same procedure is often referred to as a Cloze task in the literature, citing Taylor 1953
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's central adjective is one the systems it is compared against also use.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison of bidirectional models: the authors distinguish their deep bidirectional pre-training from a shallow concatenation of independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left language models, so the word alone does not separate the architectures
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the Cloze task of Taylor 1953 - delete a word from a passage and ask a reader to supply it - made the pre-training objective of a transformer language model as the masked language model

span.label: bidirectional - TWO ARCHITECTURES UNDER ONE WORD, SEPARATED BY THE AUTHORS: for ELMo it is the concatenation of two independently trained one-directional models, which this paper calls a shallow concatenation and elsewhere 'not deeply bidirectional'; for BERT it is a single model conditioned on both sides at once - so the adjective names a property of the training objective in one case and of the output vector in the other
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: masked LM - THE PAPER'S NAME FOR A TASK THE LITERATURE ALREADY NAMED: the authors say outright that the procedure is often referred to as a Cloze task, citing Taylor 1953, so the 2018 name and the 1953 name denote one procedure and the field kept the newer one
